artifacts.synopsis: A BCO 40-5 citation arose from Metro New York Presbytery's failure to redress a session that allowed a woman to expound Scripture in place of the sermon preceding the Lord's Supper, held services without preaching, and celebrated the Supper without a preceding sermon. The SJC remitted the matter to the presbytery for constitutional resolution because the session's later no-exception response was clearly inadequate and the unapproved minutes were unclear. Presbytery must complete its work with TE Higgins and Trinity Presbyterian Church's session and report to the 51st General Assembly. A separate procedural note questioned the Assembly's direct referral but did not void it.

artifacts.title: BCO 40-5 Matter re NW Georgia
artifacts.synopsis: Presbytery approved calls and installed three associate pastors after a constitutionally deficient election. The SJC found egregious error, including slate voting, a standing rather than ballot vote, and failure to determine and record the number of voters present under the then-current rule. It nevertheless denied the requested annulment of the installations because PCA judicial proceedings supplied no precedent and the remedy's legitimacy was doubtful. The SJC stayed further proceedings and declared the report concluded.

The General Assembly's powers are enumerated in BCO 14-6 and include the following:

artifacts.synopsis: Biese and others complained that Tennessee Valley Presbytery erred by approving Redeemer Church session minutes without exception—minutes noting a youth Super Bowl party—and by denying their complaint seeking a Sabbath exception. The SJC denied the complaint: because Presbytery gave no reasons for its actions, the record was insufficient to find it erred in interpreting the Constitution. A concurrence said the denial did not decide the Sabbath merits; a dissent would have held the complaint judicially out of order for lack of SJC jurisdiction over presbytery record review.

artifacts.synopsis: After her session erased her from the roll, Anna Lewis filed a BCO 40-5 report directly with the SJC, alleging the Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley failed to redress the session's alleged failure to give BCO 38-4 notice. The SJC held the filing out of order: under RAO 16-10.c and OMSJC Chapter 15, BCO Chapter 40 matters come to it only by General Assembly referral. It did not decide the merits, but noted that without proper notice Lewis remains a member unless she joined another church. Dissents disputed that limitation and cited past direct reviews.

Moreover, the SJC's stated concern was that the Record needed to show “how Presbytery understood these statements,” and whether Presbytery required or received from the teaching elder the kinds of expanded explanations noted in the five areas set forth above.

artifacts.synopsis: An SJC complaint alleged that Ohio Valley Presbytery failed to comply with the SJC's prior remand in Case 2014-01, which required it to 'hear further' from TE Charles Hickey about his changed view on Larger Catechism 177. The SJC denied the complaint. It held that the prior decision neither sustained nor denied the original complaint and prescribed no particular examination procedure; Hickey's nine pages of additional affirmations, exegesis, and answers constituted hearing further, and he addressed the five identified areas at least in part. A concurrence believed the SJC could also have adjudicated the confessional-difference merits; a dissent would have found noncompliance and reached the merits.

artifacts.title: Brown v. Northern California Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Northern California Presbytery adopted an abstract resolution declaring six different views on the diaconate permissible for ministers and Sessions; the SJC sustained the complaints and annulled the resolution, holding that no court may issue binding abstract decrees beyond its proper jurisdictional exercise. A concurring opinion analyzed each of the six diaconal views in detail and set out standards (the GUMP/Kniseley framework) for when diaconal assistant practices are constitutionally permissible.

artifacts.synopsis: Louisiana Presbytery’s refusal to institute process after examining Steve Wilkins’s Federal Vision teachings was challenged for applying the wrong constitutional standard and overlooking a strong presumption that some views were out of conformity with the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s denial. A “difference” need not expressly contradict the Standards; Presbytery must independently investigate and classify it rather than accept the member’s assurance or shift the burden to objectors. The ruling did not adjudicate Wilkins’s guilt; the Central Carolina memorial remained before the SJC.

artifacts.synopsis: In a BCO 40-5 memorial, Central Carolina Presbytery alleged that Louisiana Presbytery had exonerated TE J. Steven Wilkins despite his published views on election, the church, perseverance, assurance, and baptism allegedly contradicting the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the memorial’s gravity and found Presbytery failed to show due diligence, ordering a recorded examination, formal responses, and report. Presbytery later met the procedural directives, but the SJC relied on Case 2007-8’s substantive finding, cited Presbytery under BCO 40-5, and appointed a prosecutor for Case 2007-14.
